summary: Noice's comeback C64 demo, coded by Shadow with graphics by Archmage and music by Dane, which placed third in the C64 demo compo at Little Computer People 2008.
why: Several sceners thought it should have won. They single out Archmage's consistent graphics, the tunnel and vectors, and the smooth overall design and flow, even if the effects themselves aren't new for the C64.

quote.text: The effects aren't new for the C64 but the overall design, flow and smoothness give me that feel-good feeling.

summary: Focus's monochrome concept demo for the C64, placed 5th in the demo compo at X 2001: a black-and-white room with a sofa, captioned with everyday ways of wasting time, set to Mindflow's ambient music.
why: Sceners single out the minimal black-and-white design and Mindflow's music, and hold it up as proof that a demo can work without heavy effects. It was later remade for the ZX Spectrum and released as PC and Mac screensavers.

quote.text: More proof that you don't need raster-killing effects and ugly routines to make an excellent demo.

summary: Camelot's C64 demo, placed third in the C64 demo compo at Little Computer People 2011. Code by Cruzer, graphics by BizKid and Cruzer, music by Jeff with guest tunes from DRAX and 4-Mat.
why: Sceners single out the effects: an unlimited-bobs routine with unusually many frames, colourful Kefrens bars, a zoomer behind a sprite stencil, and a 1536-dot part. Several said it looked like an Amiga demo. Some found the graphics and linking weaker, and it's short.

quote.text: I realize that perhaps some of these effects are not totally impossible to do, but you have managed to make them alot more beautiful than anyone else before.

summary: Alone Coder's ZX Spectrum 48K demo with AY music, which came second in the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at Forever 2013.
why: A runner-up at Forever 2013 that sticks to the stock 48K Spectrum. The video credits it to Alone Coder and friends.
highlights: graveyard picture with a glowing orb

summary: Mad Team's Atari 8-bit demo that won the Atari demo compo at Forever 2009, with code by Tebe, graphics by Ooz and music by stRing.
why: A compo winner at Forever 2009. The stills show large hand-drawn pictures by Ooz built around a stage magician, carrying the prod visually.

summary: Focus's C64 demo by Ben (code) and Hein (music and graphics) that won the demo compo at X 2004: abstract, minimal design built from impossible isometric shapes, circles and squares.
why: Sceners single out Hein's GoatTracker soundtrack and the fresh, different design, with the isometric impossible shapes and the Tetris part drawing particular praise.

quote.text: WHAT A DESIGN! It's always good to see something totally different. Love it!

summary: Crest's Commodore 64 demo that needs a 16MB REU, streaming full-colour NUFLI animations from the expansion memory. It won the Console/Real Wild compo at Breakpoint 2010.
why: Sceners praised the technical side and the colourful animated screens, including a seamlessly looped underwater animation. A Rick Astley rickroll gave it what one commenter called a very high crowdpleaser factor.

quote.text: Obviously a lot of work went into this, and it was a joy being rickrolled after for a second actually believing this finally was "Meet Crest". :-)

summary: Performers' four-disk-side C64 demo that won the demo compo at X 2023, with a large crew of coders and guest artists, music from dEViLOCk, Jammer, Linus and LMan, and a part replaying 100 classic games.
why: Winner of what sceners call perhaps the strongest C64 demo compo ever, and of Best Oldschool Production at the Meteoriks 2024. Comments single out the 100-games part, Bitbreaker's vector scenes, the music and the humour.

quote.text: The 100games-part stood out. This is not only a demo-part, this is digital art taken to some uber-next level.

summary: Bay 6's ZX Spectrum demo written in BASIC, which won the ZX-Basic compo at Base-X 2015. Code and graphics by Diver, AY music by Nik-O. The video is the party version.
why: A compo-winning demo for the Spectrum's built-in BASIC, inspired by Haujobb's You Should. Worth watching to see what Diver got out of a language not known for speed.

summary: Entire's ZX Spectrum 128K demo that won the demo compo at ZX AAA Compo 2013, with code and music by Rob F. and graphics by Mellona and NINBER.
why: A compo winner that makes use of the Spectrum's multicolour mode, according to its tags, and it was made with the Pentagon clone in mind.
highlights: music by Rob F. and Fine Soft.

summary: Thesuper's ZX Spectrum 128K demo that won the Combined 8-Bit Demo compo at DiHalt 2012, mixing comic-style story screens with isometric graphics and particle effects.
why: A compo winner at DiHalt 2012 from a large Thesuper crew, with code by drwho and Lovebeam, graphics by Sweetbutt and music by Nick Roll.

summary: Pex Mahoney Tufvesson's C64 demo, made with Uwe 'THCM' Anfang on SID research, placed 4th in the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2014. It pairs long, clean sample playback with glitchy character-mode visuals, an a cappella quartet part and a scroller.
why: Sceners single out the sample quality, calling it the cleanest they had heard on the SID, along with the a cappella part and the scrolltext. The crowd at the party reportedly went wild for it.

quote.text: Incredible sound quality. I'm looking forward to finding out how this works. Also: best scrolltext ever.

summary: A ZX Spectrum 128 4K intro by Darklite and Offence, with code by Neon, music by Response and graphics by Pal. It came second in the Oldskool 4K Intro compo at Revision Online 2021.
why: A 4K intro that placed second at Revision and was nominated for Best Oldschool Production at The Meteoriks 2022.

summary: A ZX Spectrum 48K demo by Hooy-Program and Agenda, with code by Alone Coder, Hellboj and Szuwarek, music by Yerzmyey and graphics by Piesiu and Aki. It won the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Forever 2011.
why: A compo winner at Forever 2011 and a cross-group collaboration. It is worth a look for its chunky, colourful attribute-style effects on a stock 48K-class machine with AY music.

summary: Fairlight's C64 art demo by Hollowman (code and graphics) with music from guest Goto80, winner of the Oldschool Demo compo at Edison 2016. Poetic text screens alternate with dithered bitmaps and animated effects.
why: Sceners welcomed it as Hollowman's long-awaited return, praising the mood and how well Goto80's soundtrack fits the visuals. One commenter notes it is in memory of text-adventure author Paul Panks. Some found the text parts slow.

quote.text:
Excellent in all possible ways. Narrative and emotional expressions, 
accompanied with beautiful music.

summary: Resurrection's Atari 8-bit demo, coded by Lak with graphics by Powrooz and music by PG, which came second in the Atari demo compo at Forever 2008.
why: A podium finish at Forever 2008. It opens on a detailed hand-drawn title picture of a woman and a yellow taxi against a city skyline.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by Fourth Dimension and Triebkraft that won the ZX Spectrum demo compo at DiHalt 2007, built around a cartoon kid and a star.
why: A compo winner at DiHalt 2007. The stills show hand-drawn monochrome cartoon scenes mixed with wireframe vector shapes.

summary: Fairlight's two-disk-side C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2012, with vector parts, a zoomer, a plasma-style interference effect and a "turn disk" picture of a punk girl.
why: Sceners single out the 16-colour plasma/interference effect, the transitions and the music, with Wiklund's second tune drawing particular praise, along with graphics by Louie and Prowler.

quote.text: A lot of great effects, tied together by fitting transitions and great music.

summary: Hitmen's C64 demo, coded and designed by Groepaz with music by Moog and Xiny6581 and graphics by Cupid and Death, which came third in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2013.
why: Sceners single out the physics parts, with falling blocks and fluid effects, and a marching squares part at the end. Several call it a coder's demo that brings effects to the C64 which hadn't been done before.

quote.text: i LOVED the physics part. It is just wonderful. I could have watched that way longer.

summary: Slight's Atari 8-bit demo that won the Atari 8bit demo compo at QuaST 1995, with code by Seban, Soused Teat, Rzóg and The Last Byte, and graphics by PW and Dracon.
why: A compo winner from the mid-90s Polish Atari scene. Its tags point to a dancer, morphing, a zoomer and a scroller, and it is noted for the 'stickman's world' theme.

summary: Triebkraft and 4th Dimension's ZX Spectrum demo, which won the 8 bit 640Kb Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2004.
why: A compo winner at one of the main Russian Spectrum parties, and a joint production between two groups.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by Schafft and Hedj that placed third in the ZX Spectrum 640K Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2015.
why: It was nominated for Best Low-End Demo at The Meteoriks 2016, a sign of standing well beyond its compo placing.

summary: Offence and Prosonix's four-disk-side C64 demo, placed fourth in the C64 demo compo at Little Computer People 2011. It runs as a string of press-space parts, opening with a 2001: A Space Odyssey style intro featuring a talking HAL eye.
why: A Scene.org Awards nominee that sceners call a huge, graphics-heavy throwback to the late-80s megademo. They single out the film-like 2001 intro, the Tron part, the scene heroes part and the large vertical twister.

quote.text: I didn't think I'd ever be impressed by a demo again like I was in 1988-90. But I was wrong. This is outstanding.

summary: Resource and Coma's two-disk-side C64 trackmo, third in the C64 demo compo at The Party 1997, with code by Edhellon and Oswald, graphics by Tyrant and Splash, and music from Da Blondie plus guests Eclipse and Taki.
why: Sceners call it an overlooked favourite: fast-paced, colourful effects, strong graphics and fonts, and nice transitions that still look modern. Even the compo winner's member admits Void deserved the win.

quote.text: Great music, beautiful and colourful effects and graphics, many fresh new ideas with nice transitions. And quite long.

summary: Extend's C64 demo from X 2016, coded by Barfly and Mankeli with graphics by Duce and Electric and a Barracuda soundtrack. It placed 18th in the demo compo after being shown last, following a break.
why: Sceners widely call it underrated for its placing, praising the fresh hires pixel work, the psychedelic atmosphere and Barracuda's techno SID tune. Several rank it among the best at X 2016.

quote.text: The music and visuals create an atmosphere like nothing else in the competition.  Excellent pixels, fantastic looking effects and great music!

summary: Stardust's ZX Spectrum demo that placed 2nd in the ZX Spectrum demo compo at CAFe 2019: ABBA-style silhouettes and dance animations cut tightly to a gabber soundtrack by Nik-O.
why: Tagged for extreme sync between music and visuals, it pairs ABBA imagery with gabber. A writeup on how it was made is available in Russian.

summary: An Amstrad CPC demo by Benediction and Arkos that came second in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision Online 2021, with code by Krusty and Eliot, music by Targhan and graphics by Voxy and Tom et Jerry.
why: A podium finish at Revision's oldskool compo and a nomination for Best Oldschool Production at The Meteoriks 2022 put it among the year's stand-out 8-bit demos.

summary: Scoopex's ZX Spectrum demo that won the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Forever 2019, with code by Mr. Spiv and lordcoxis, music by LaesQ and graphics by Pheel, Xile and K-0s.
why: A Forever compo winner that uses the Spectrum's multicolour mode to get more colour onto the screen than the stock attribute grid usually allows.

summary: A ZX Spectrum 128K demo by g0blinish that won the Retro Demo compo at Demosplash 2014, framed as a television set with a screen showing changing pictures and effects.
why: It took first place in the Retro Demo competition at Demosplash 2014, beating entries from other retro platforms.

summary: Booze Design's two-disk-side C64 demo with a Western theme, winner of the demo compo at Fjälldata 2025. Effects-heavy parts by a large coding team, set among colourful hand-drawn pictures by Mirage, Archmage and Dane.
why: Won Best Oldschool Production at The Meteoriks 2026. Sceners single out the VIC trickery and the way the code serves the graphics; coders admit to watching it in a debugger to work out how it's done.

quote.text: even better: the code seems to 100% serve the beauty. to me this is the most important achievement

summary: Booze Design's C64 demo by HCL and Dane that won the C64 demo compo at Deadline 2005: a slow, design-led run of Japanese-themed parts, layered shapes and big pictures in XFLI and IFLI.
why: Sceners single out its calm pacing, Dane's music and graphics that some call among the best on the C64, with clever layer techniques hidden under the design. Many keep coming back to it years later.

quote.text: it is a true peace of art.. it is so peaceful, so relaxing, serene..

summary: Hitmen's C64 demo from X 2016, where it placed 7th: a long run of effects parts with graphics by Carrion, Se7en, Peacemaker and Cupid, code by Groepaz, HCL and Peacemaker, and music by Linus.
why: Sceners praise its polish, flow and graphics throughout, and the soundtrack gets repeated praise. Several feel it deserved a far higher compo placing. Commenters single out the ice effect in the intro and ending, and the shadow-casting routine.
highlights: ice effect in intro and ending

quote.text: it's seriously polished from back to front and it never gets boring because of it. not to mention the proper flow, superb gfx throughout and brilliant soundtrack.

summary: A four-disk-side C64 demo from Fairlight, Prosonix and Offence that came third in the demo compo at X 2012, opening with a Star Wars-themed section and moving through scrollers, a huge picture upscroller and a credits part.
why: Sceners single out the sheer amount of pixel art from Pal, the smooth Star Wars scroller and the atmospheric end credits. Some found it too long, but its scope is the point.

quote.text: Pal, you are a pixel animal. Bringing us this unfuckingbelievable amount of finest pixel art in just one demo.

summary: Samar's C64 demo, the 100% final version of I Love The Cube, coded by Mr Wegi with music by Conrad and graphics by Isildur and Conrad. Cube-themed vector parts over hi-res pictures such as the lollipop girl.
why: Sceners praise the big vectors, the dot-plotter scrollers and Conrad's music, and many felt this final version was a clear step up from the party release. Its sense of humour gets a mention too.

quote.text: Amazingly smooth and stylish demo, respect to the Samar guys!

summary: Kkolor is a ZX Spectrum demo by Triebkraft and 4th Dimension. It won the 8 Bit 640Kb Demo compo at Chaos Constructions 2005, with code by psndcj, graphics by pROF, Diver and G.D., and music by C-jeff, Fatal Snipe and Key-Jee.
why: A first-place winner at Chaos Constructions 2005, one of the main Russian Spectrum parties. Two well-known Spectrum groups made it together, and it fills the screen with bold blocks of colour.

summary: The final version of Censor Design and Oxyron's big multi-disk C64 demo, with fixes over the 2014 release and a large team of coders, graphicians and musicians.
why: Sceners single out the music, especially the main tune on disk 1, the smooth effects and Mirage's big scrolling owl logo. Several call it one of the best C64 demos they've seen.
highlights: flying bee parts with zooming gfx

quote.text: The music in this one is superb, main tune on disk 1 may be one of the best demo-tunes ever made (imo).

summary: A 1K intro for the Commodore 64 by 4mat, released at Forever 2006, where it won the Commodore 1K Intro competition. Symmetrical, colourful chunky patterns grow and shift to a beat.
why: Sceners praise its fluid visuals and stomping beat squeezed into 1K, with one noting a Psychedelia influence. 4mat later released the source in DASM format.

quote.text: Love the Psychedelia influence.  Very fluid visuals and a stomping beat - all in 1k.

summary: Viznut's C64 4K intro for Pers' Wastaiset Produktiot, winner of the C64 4K intro compo at Breakpoint 2010: a wordless story told with only three big pixels moving in sync with the music.
why: Sceners single out how much storytelling it gets out of almost nothing and how tightly the pixels' movements are synced to Viznut's music. Many read it as a boy-meets-girl relationship with no happy ending.

quote.text: Incredible what little requires for storytelling.

summary: A ZX Spectrum demo by 4th Dimension and Triebkraft, released at Chaos Constructions 2006, where it placed third in the 8-bit 640k demo compo.
why: A podium finish at one of the main Russian Spectrum parties from a collaboration between two groups. The video shows a dithered portrait set beside colourful animated effects.

summary: Resource and The Dreams' C64 demo that came third in the demo compo at X 2004, with code by Bubis, Ninja and Oswald, graphics by AmN, Leon and Sander, and music by GRG.
why: Sceners single out the fast bitmap and maths effects, especially a smooth-running Julia fractal and huge vectors bigger than the screen, along with GRG's energetic soundtrack. Some felt it looked unfinished, but most enjoyed it.

quote.text: My favorites are the vectors inside vectors and that Juhlia, wow! (Not many times I had seen a decent running Juhlia in any 8bit machine. Perhaps 1 or 2 times only).

summary: Hooy-Program's ZX Spectrum demo, coded, drawn and scored by Gasman, which took second place in the ZX Spectrum Demo compo at Forever 2023.
why: A one-person production that placed second at Forever and made the Meteoriks 2024 watchlist.

summary: Fairlight and Genesis Project's two-disk-side C64 demo that won the demo compo at Fjälldata 2026: a conjuring-trick themed show built around Redcrab's animated PETSCII, border sprite effects and a nod to LFT's demo 9.
why: Sceners single out Redcrab's PETSCII animation as some of the best ever made on the C64, alongside border tricks and an all-border upscroller at the end that even other coders found hard to explain.

quote.text: it's the animation that stands out most - because I don't think this quality of animation has been done on C64 before

summary: UKScene Allstars' ZX Spectrum demo, coded and scored by Gasman with graphics by Equinox, that won the Oldskool Demo compo at Sundown 2006. It opens on a mock platform-game title screen.
why: A compo winner at Sundown 2006 against oldskool entries from other machines, and a showcase for Equinox's colourful Spectrum graphics alongside Gasman's code and music.

summary: A 4K intro for the Amstrad CPC by Hooy-Program and Benediction, with code by Krusty, graphics by Voxy and music by Aki. It placed third in the Oldskool 4K Intro compo at Revision 2012.
why: A podium finish at Revision in the oldskool 4K category, and the source is available for anyone curious how it fits in the size limit.

summary: Dirty Minds' 1K intro for the Amstrad CPC, coded by Optimus, which won the combined demo/intro compo at ReSeT 2014. It renders a voxel landscape in dithered blocks inside a small window.
why: A voxel landscape squeezed into 1K on a stock CPC, and it took first place at ReSeT 2014. The source is available for anyone curious how it fits.

summary: Dirty Minds' 4K intro for the Amstrad CPC, coded by Optimus with music by Aki. It placed second in the Demo compo at ReSeT (.fr) 2012.
why: A size-limited CPC intro that held its own against full demos, taking second place in the Demo competition at ReSeT 2012.

summary: Offence's C64 demo, coded, drawn and scored by Kristian Myklebust with a bob part by Geir Ytterdahl, placed 2nd in the Oldskool Demo compo at Solskogen 2013. Flat-colour silhouettes and landscapes move to a minimalist tune.
why: Sceners praise its catchy demo flow, the minimalist jew's harp music synced to the action, the airplane scene and the fact that it loops endlessly. It went down well at the party itself.

quote.text: It has a really nice and catchy demo flow. The Music is also extremely nice and special. It works very well with the action on-screen, and the synchronizations with the airplane etc - really great.

summary: Horizon's C64 demo, the last one from the group, which won the C64 demo compo at Hurricane and Brutal Summer Party 1992. It mixes filled and morphing vectors, a raytraced part and atmospheric graphics, with music by Boogaloo and Bappalander.
why: Sceners single out the smooth filled and glenz vectors, the morphing hidden-line objects and the raytracer, all remarkable for 1992. Some credit it with introducing the techniques later used for filled vectors on the C64.

quote.text: Must have seen the vector part a hundred times. It was the first filled vectors I ever saw on a C64. Morphing! Glenz! Come on! And smooth as well.

summary: Progress's ZX Spectrum 128K demo, winner of the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Enlight 1997, with code and graphics shared across Fux, Mic, Rom, Kolver and KSA.
why: It won its compo at Enlight 1997, and it is tagged for the Spectrum's multicolour mode. The stills show large, grotesque hand-drawn pictures such as a screaming face with a gun to its head and a bloodshot eyeball.

summary: Fairlight's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Datastorm 2017 Summer, with code by moh, Hollowman and Pantaloon and music by Wiklund. A quick-paced run of full-screen effects ending in an endless loop.
why: Sceners single out Wiklund's soundtrack, the pacing and transitions so smooth you forget they are transitions. The fractal zoom and the tunnel also get repeated mentions.

quote.text: Really nice and smooth demo, with very nice transitions, so seamless that you forget it actually is a transition.
